title: Configuration Options
description: Master configuration and options patterns in ASP.NET Core.

data.text: The **Options pattern** provides a strongly-typed way to access configuration settings. Instead of reading raw strings from `IConfiguration`, you bind a section to a plain C# class and inject the bound instance into your services.

data.title: Why use the Options pattern?
data.text: Strongly-typed settings give you IntelliSense, compile-time safety, easier unit testing, and natural integration with DI, validation, and hot-reload.

rows: Read-only settings that never change at runtime.
Per-request settings that need to refresh when appsettings.json changes.
Long-lived services that watch for config changes and react to them.

terms.definition: Singleton wrapper around a settings instance. Best for immutable configuration.
Scoped, recomputed per request. Supports live reload of appsettings.json.
Singleton that watches for changes and raises a OnChange callback.
Extension that runs DataAnnotation attributes (Required, Range, etc.) on the settings class.
Forces validation at startup so the app fails fast on misconfiguration.

data.title: Reacting to live config changes
data.content: Use IOptionsMonitor to react when appsettings.json changes on disk.

cards.title: IOptions<T>
cards.description: Read once, used for the lifetime of the app.

cards.title: IOptionsSnapshot<T>
cards.description: Re-read per request from the latest configuration.

cards.title: IOptionsMonitor<T>
cards.description: Singleton wrapper that raises OnChange callbacks.
cons: Slightly more code to manage the change token

data.title: Don't inject IOptions<T> into a singleton if you need reloads
data.text: IOptions<T> snapshots the value at first construction. If a singleton needs to react to changes, inject IOptionsMonitor<T> instead.

items.text: Bind every section to a strongly-typed POCO.
Annotate required and bounded fields with DataAnnotations.
Call ValidateOnStart() so the app fails fast on bad config.
Use IOptions<T> for singletons that don't need reloads.
Use IOptionsMonitor<T> when you need to react to live changes.

data.title: Add options to an existing API
data.description: Refactor an existing controller to read settings via the Options pattern.
steps: Create a `JwtSettings` class with Issuer, Audience, and SigningKey properties.
Inject `IOptions<JwtSettings>` into a controller and expose a debug endpoint that returns the bound values (omit the key in real apps).
Change a value in appsettings.json, restart, and confirm the new value is reflected.
data.expectedOutcome: The endpoint returns configuration values without ever reading `IConfiguration` directly, and the app refuses to launch if a required field is missing.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The Options pattern turns configuration into strongly-typed POCOs.
IOptions<T> is singleton, IOptionsSnapshot<T> is scoped and reloads, IOptionsMonitor<T> is singleton and reactive.
DataAnnotations + ValidateOnStart give you fail-fast configuration.
Live reload works out of the box for appsettings.json when you use Snapshot or Monitor.
Avoid scattering `IConfiguration["..."]` reads across your codebase — centralize with options.
data.takeaway: The Options pattern makes configuration type-safe, validated, and easy to test.
